source: NCERT Class IX, India and the Contemporary World I, History Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. The Weimar Republic and its Problems
points: After losing **World War I (1918)**, Germany became a democratic republic — the **Weimar Republic**.
The harsh **Treaty of Versailles (1919)** blamed Germany for the war, took its colonies and territory, imposed a huge **war indemnity** and disarmed it → deep national **humiliation and anger**.
The **Great Economic Depression (1929)** caused mass **unemployment and hyperinflation**, discrediting the Weimar democracy.

sections.heading: 2. The Rise of Hitler
points: **Adolf Hitler** led the **Nazi Party (National Socialist Party)**, promising to restore Germany's pride and end the Versailles injustice.
In **1933**, Hitler became **Chancellor**; he then destroyed democracy — the **Enabling Act (1933)** gave him **dictatorial powers**.
He built a **totalitarian state**: all other parties banned, the **secret police (Gestapo)**, propaganda controlled by **Goebbels**.
The **Nazi state promoted its image** through mass rallies, radio, film and posters.

sections.heading: 3. Nazi Ideology and the Holocaust
points: Nazism preached **racism** — belief in a superior **'Aryan' race** and hatred of **Jews (anti-Semitism)**, Roma, disabled people and others.
Jews were persecuted (**Nuremberg Laws**), confined to **ghettos and concentration camps**.
The **Holocaust** — the mass murder of about **six million Jews** and others in camps like **Auschwitz** — was Nazism's most horrific crime.
Hitler's aggression triggered **World War II (1939)**; Germany was defeated in **1945**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Weimar Republic after WWI; Treaty of Versailles (1919) = harsh (indemnity, lost territory) → resentment.
Great Depression 1929 → unemployment → Nazism rose.
Hitler = Nazi Party; Chancellor 1933; Enabling Act (dictatorial powers).
Gestapo (secret police); Goebbels (propaganda); 'Aryan' race myth; anti-Semitism.
Holocaust = ~6 million Jews murdered (Auschwitz); WWII began 1939, Germany defeated 1945.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Treaty of Versailles (1919)** humiliated Germany — a key cause of Nazism's rise.
The **Enabling Act (1933)** gave Hitler **dictatorial** powers, ending democracy.
**Propaganda** was led by **Goebbels**; the secret police was the **Gestapo**.
The **Holocaust** targeted **Jews** and other minorities.
